What are the consequences of fabricated polarizations for Iran?🔹Reducing the country's complex issues to binaries like "peace-seeking vs. warmongering" or "negotiation vs. war" can steer society away from a genuine conversation about national interests, costs, and foreign policy options.🔹Critics of this approach argue that negotiation should be a tool of foreign policy, not the only solution; just as defense and deterrence capabilities should not be equated with "warmongering."🔹The experience of the JCPOA and America's withdrawal from it has brought into sharper focus the debate over guaranteeing an agreement's implementation, reciprocal concessions, and preserving bargaining power. The experience of past agreements has also shown that an agreement alone, without guarantees of implementation and bargaining power, does not necessarily lead to a sustainable outcome.🔹When individuals and factions are categorized with labels like "warmonger" or "peacenik," the possibility of rational dialogue about details diminishes.🔹From the perspective of critics of polarization, a society that can discuss its differences while emphasizing shared national interests will have a greater capacity to manage foreign crises.@Farspolitics - link

🔹The platform says restrictions imposed by the Economic Security Police and some related bodies have made it difficult to access part of its reserves and fulfill its obligations to users.

🔹These concerns come as, under Central Bank regulations, online platforms must hold reserves equivalent to their obligations for gold sold, and the stored gold must be converted into standard bars with a purity of at least 995 within three months.

🔸Now, given recent concerns about users' access to their gold and the claims raised about the backing of transactions, connecting all platforms to the supervisory system as quickly as possible — with online reporting of their inventory and obligations — has become more important than ever and could ease some of users' concerns.

False cheating accusations against students due to software errors

🔹AI detectors used to identify cheating among school and university students have come under scrutiny in new research for significant errors, in some cases mistakenly flagging completely human-written text as AI-generated.

🔹Investigations show these tools do not detect the true origin of the text; instead, they calculate the probability of AI-generated text based on statistical features and writing style.

🔹In one experiment, a completely human-written text was assessed by 5 commercial tools as anywhere from "zero percent" to "100 percent" AI-generated.

🔹These systems have also been reported to make more errors with people whose first language is not English; in a study of 91 real TOEFL essays, an average of 61 percent of human-written texts were mistakenly identified as AI-generated.

🔹Following these problems, universities such as Waterloo in Canada and Cape Town have stopped using Turnitin's AI detection score and have emphasized relying on evidence such as drafts, edit history, learning process, and conversations with the student.

@Farsna - Link

Yet according to explicit statements by Mohsen Rezaei and Baghaei, Iran's conditions had already been conveyed to America through mediators last week. It is also abundantly clear that holding a meeting with the American side — especially at the United Nations — affects oil prices and reduces that pressure. If America has not yet sent an official response through mediators accepting all of Iran's conditions, what is the necessity of holding such a meeting and bearing its side effects — the reduction of oil prices and, consequently, the reduction of pressure on America?

Therefore, America needs to bring oil prices down somewhat — even slightly — before taking action, so that afterward, despite the oil shock, the final price does not reach an unexpected figure. Thus, any action that leads to a reduction in oil prices at the current time inadvertently facilitates America's pre-attack needs. The question for the Foreign Minister is: why was the meeting with Witkoff held at such a decisive time?

Yashar and Farnaz, in pursuit of scapegoating Iran
🔹In the middle of his exposé clip about the trusts, Yashar Soltani — without mentioning America's prior violations — names the Stability political faction as the cause of the understanding's collapse.
🔹This is the same narrative previously put forward in Farnaz Fassihi's report in the New York Times; a narrative claiming that the action of a rogue group in Iran destroyed the diplomatic opportunity that existed in the understanding between Iran and America.
But what is the hidden reality?
🔹The most important clause of the understanding was the acceptance of Iranian arrangements in the administration of the strait. That is, in exchange for accepting certain obligations, Iran had secured its right to manage and maintain its own particular arrangements in the world's most important oil passage.
🔹From day one, America was determined to violate this clause and, as with the violation of other clauses, to normalize it. The failure to release the assets and the failure to establish a ceasefire on other fronts are clear examples of these violations.
🔹Logically, Iran, in defense of its gains under the understanding, should have shown itself to be serious and, during the transitional period, should have stood firm on its rights so that it could secure its right in the final agreement.
🔹The opening of the southern corridor in the strait was a fundamental violation of the understanding by America — an action that, if left unanswered, would have practically rendered the main clause of the understanding ineffective.
🔹After several days of warnings, the timely action of striking the vessels and not remaining indifferent to the violation of Iran's rights under the understanding was defensible on the part of the country's decision-makers.
🔹The inverted narrative of the story that portrays Iran as responsible for disrupting the understanding is fabricated by Israeli and monarchist accounts and American media.
Why is this narrative important?
🔸If this reading is correct, what happened in the Strait of Hormuz was a reaction to America's clear violation of the understanding.
🔸In this framework, the one who first broke the understanding was Washington, not Iran. But the rival narrative, by swapping the roles of victim and culprit, wants to shift the political cost of this decision onto an internal faction.
🔸The narrative that "the rogues broke the understanding" is on the surface simple and attractive, but when placed alongside America's chain of violations, it collapses.
🖼The important question, however, is why should one expect Iran to remain a spectator in the face of the violation of the main clause of the understanding? And why now, instead of condemning the primary violator, is the finger of accusation pointed inward?
